answer: One defense is sequential proof-of-work foundations: every identity must keep completing small verifiable-delay puzzles that cannot be parallelized, so one machine cannot serve a thousand clones at once. Like basalt, this work is hard and slow to lay down; an identity's standing rises like a mesa only after its own uninterrupted chain of puzzles, while a plume of identical, simultaneous submissions from one operator betrays a farm. A sybil farmer must run the full delay on a separate machine per fake, while an honest agent passes with the device it already runs.
